name: Regulatory effects

subjectOf.text: Private fund advisers increasingly factor the regulatory structure into decisions about the size of their assets under management, a shift partly explained by the higher post-Dodd-Frank cost structure, since higher AUM and the corresponding fee revenue can offset higher compliance costs.
subjectOf.abstract: Private fund advisers are increasingly taking the regulatory structure into account in determining their AUM. This can par- tially be explained with the higher overall post-Dodd-Frank-Act cost structure for the industry, which is shown in Figures 6, 8, and 9.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Post Dodd-Frank Act Evolution of the Private Fund Industry Comparative Evidence from 2012 and 2 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2739479

subjectOf.text: Sensitivity to the Form PF quarterly reporting threshold rose sharply: only 19 percent of 2012 respondents took the $1.5 billion threshold into account, compared with 33 percent in 2015.
subjectOf.abstract: In 2012, only 19% of respondents took the Form PF quar- terly threshold into account, whereas 33% of respondents in 2015 found the threshold relevant.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Post Dodd-Frank Act Evolution of the Private Fund Industry Comparative Evidence from 2012 and 2 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2739479
scope_conditions: the $1.5 billion Form PF quarterly reporting threshold

subjectOf.text: A majority of respondents in both surveys, 76.1 percent in 2012 and 65 percent in 2015, believed the Dodd-Frank Act did not affect their reporting funds' earnings.
subjectOf.abstract: Figure 16 illustrates that the majority of survey respondents in both the 2012 survey (76.1%) and 2015 survey (65%) believed that the Dodd-Frank Act did not affect reporting funds' earnings.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Post Dodd-Frank Act Evolution of the Private Fund Industry Comparative Evidence from 2012 and 2 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2739479
scope_conditions: perceived effect on fund earnings, not measured returns

subjectOf.text: Even though the Dodd-Frank Act's overall regulatory impact on the private fund industry was low, the compliance costs generated by the evolving regulatory environment carry many unexpected consequences with the potential to further reshape industry practices.
subjectOf.abstract: Despite the low regulatory impact of the Dodd-Frank Act overall, this article indicates that compliance costs associated with the evolving regulatory environment for private fund advisers have many unexpected consequences that could have the potential to further shape industry practices.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Post Dodd-Frank Act Evolution of the Private Fund Industry Comparative Evidence from 2012 and 2 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2739479

subjectOf.text: The comparative evidence suggests the long-term effects of the evolving post-Dodd-Frank regulatory environment may be more substantial than either the industry or regulators initially anticipated.
subjectOf.abstract: The comparative evidence in this study suggests that long-term ef- fects of the evolving post-Dodd-Frank-Act regulatory environment might be more substantial than the industry and regulators initially anticipated.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Post Dodd-Frank Act Evolution of the Private Fund Industry Comparative Evidence from 2012 and 2 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2739479
scope_conditions: private fund advisers and their reporting funds
based on 2015 responses citing lower returns and plans to consolidate or close funds
